justifications.durability: The deliverable is a static HTML evidence fragment whose every factual claim is recoverable from the committed fragment text, the run's gate logs (write-gate.log, write-attempt1.log, negative-control.log, verify-ids.log) and the two run files on disk; I recovered the whole read-back without the writer and it agreed. The negative control was falsified (the overwrite refusal exits 1), so the guard is shown rather than asserted. Deduction: the fragment's byte sizes and mtimes are a snapshot of /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/ids, which the plan states the facility move will rewrite when the writer moves to run files, so the numbers pin a moment under a mutable path; and the excluded-signal reasons cite prior node measurements (jtmm-sensor-channel-join constants a=-4.197, r=-0.977) that a reader must find in a sibling fragment, so the fragment's exclusion table is cited rather than self-contained.
justifications.evidence: Every quantitative claim I could reach was reproduced independently on this allocation, not taken from the node's own instrument. I opened both files with imas.DBEntry at DD 4.1.1: 101154 and 101031 each present exactly {magnetics, pf_active, pf_passive, tf, wall}; magnetics homogeneous_time=0; magnetics ip peaks 998576.2 A (101154) and 698442.1 A (101031); ip time vectors 46078 and 101031... wait; 27 flux loops and 17 poloidal probes each; 10 of 12 pf_active coils serve a current, 1 tf coil serves one. The sizes match byte-for-byte (29281489 and 28504359) and the negative control reproduces: re-running the same write without --overwrite exits 1 naming /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/ids/101154_0.nc and both files keep their size and mtime (1791352399, 1791352403). A positive control on the reader is present: the writer's own receipts and my independent imas.DBEntry read agree on the IDS set and leaf counts. Deduction: the receipts.log and write-gate.log headers record that the writer module resolved from the main checkout at rev e4177d48 (packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/pulse_writer.py), which the file-tree identity check confirms is byte-identical to the reviewed base cd0a89ba for that path, so the merged writer is what ran; the fragment's meta line cites both cd0a89ba (base) and e4177d48 (writer), which is accurate but requires reading the log header to see which tree supplied the module.
justifications.fit: The fragment parses as HTML (html.parser accepts it), carries 11 element ids, every one beginning with the node id jtfm-write-dev-pulses (zero outside the prefix, no duplicates), so sibling fragments composed into one record cannot collide on an anchor. The meta line carries the plan slug, run id and base sha as evidence metadata, matching the sibling fragments' pattern. No version tag, sprint, ticket or issue identifier appears in the body; the 'section 4' and 'type-6' references are the machine-description document and the DD differential form, not plan labels. The commit subject is conventional with a body and no trailer, and no author or AI attribution appears in the commit or the fragment.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The fragment answers the node's goal and §8's write-command context honestly and completely: it names the exact gate command and its exit code, both run files with byte sizes, both write receipts (56 time-dependent leaves and 68 excluded signals per pulse), the per-pulse leaf breakdown that reconciles with the file contents (pf_active 10 + magnetics 45 + tf 1 = 56), the OP1 phase and its five description IDSs, every excluded signal with the map's own reason, and the negative control. The dispatched literal command is recorded in the fragment as a reported deviation: it exits 1 with "setting 'machine' is not set; set --machine" because three machines are reachable in this checkout; I reproduced that exact exit and message. The deviation does not defeat the goal (produce the two run files), which is met; the deviation is disclosed, not hidden. Deduction: the node reports the as-written failure as a blocker in its manifest and follow_on, so the only residual is that the follow-on write node should name --machine, which the run already asks for.
justifications.reuse: The node reuses imas-alambic's writer for the write side and imas.DBEntry at DD 4.1.1 on the read side rather than re-deriving either, and it re-reads the writer's own receipt layout (one <ids>.nc per IDS under the shot directory, plus the flat <pulse>_<run>.nc) which the engine mandates. It adds only what the goal needs, the fragment and small probe scripts (verify_ids.py, dump_receipts.py, make_fragment.py), and changes no library code. Deduction: the read-back probe is bespoke where a shared helper would serve the sibling write nodes, but that is a pattern observation, not duplication the node could have avoided within its scope.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat 772ff1b6 and git diff --stat cd0a89ba..772ff1b6 both list exactly one file, docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-facility-mint/jtfm-write-dev-pulses.html, 269 insertions, which is the manifest's declared changed_path and within the node's declared write scope (the fragment and the figures directory). No product source and no test is touched. The only data written outside the repository is the two run files under /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/ids, the location the plan's output-layout decision names for run files. The node added no figure, which is correct for a tabular write-evidence fragment.
